survival_report.system_diagnosis: The slow-bleed problem is bigger than the emergency-stop problem. Trades held between 1 and 2 hours are the single largest money drain in the entire history of the bot: 255 of them, total loss of -0.481 SOL. That is six and a half times more damage than every emergency stop combined (-0.072 SOL). These trades win 45% of the time — the highest of any time bucket — but the winners are tiny (+6% average) while the losers run all the way to -18% on average before time-exiting. The stop-loss almost never fires on this group (only 2.7%). Meanwhile no new trades fired in the last 24 hours (bot dormant in chop/altcoin-winter). The bot itself is healthy and running.
survival_report.exit_analysis: Rolling 7 days unchanged from yesterday: 6 sells, win rate 16.7%, average win +10.7%, average loss -13.2%, R/R 0.81, stop-loss rate 66.7% (tiny sample because no new sells today). Rolling 30 days: 71 sells, win rate 38%, R/R 0.73, net -0.019 SOL, stop-loss rate 48%. Brand-new finding mined this run: by hold-time bucket, the worst cohort is 1-2 hours (R/R 0.33, -0.481 SOL); the second worst is 0-15 minutes (-0.327 SOL, instant blowups); the 0.5-1 hour bucket is third (-0.262 SOL, mostly slow-stop). Total emergency-stop damage all-time is -0.072 SOL across 28 trades — a tail-risk problem but seven times smaller than the slow-bleed problem in dollar terms.
survival_report.strategy_work: Processed three new ideas from the research brain. Confirmed the 1-2h slow-bleed cohort as the highest-value target (H6) and advanced it to READY status with backing data verified. Two of the three new ideas (copy-trade tilt cooldown and copy-trade wallet blacklist) are not actionable right now because copy-trade has been completely dormant since April 5 — zero trades in 30 days. They are parked with rules pre-written for the moment copy-trade fires again. Also independently re-ran the copy-trade tilt analysis and found the research brain's caveat was inverted: same-wallet trades after a loss are mild (-2% average), while different-wallet trades after a loss are devastating (-14% average). That means the per-wallet cooldown idea is the WRONG fix, and the global half-size after any copy-trade loss is the RIGHT fix. Permanently killed the per-wallet-cooldown variant.
survival_report.directives_changes: Bumped version to 2. Shifted current_priority focus from emergency-stop tail-risk to the much larger 1-2h slow-bleed cohort (six times more dollar damage). Added three new pending hypotheses (H5 copy-trade tilt with revised rule, H6 hold-time death zone marked READY, H7 wallet blacklist parked dormant). Added H8 instrumentation hypothesis: the bot needs to log the peak price reached during each trade so future backtests of breakeven-floor and partial-take-profit rules become possible. Added copy_trade itself to the active_strategies list with DORMANT status (it was missing from run-276's list). Added a permanent killed-idea entry for the per-wallet-cooldown variant.

changelog: Identified the slowest-bleed problem in the trade history: trades held between 1 and 2 hours have a 45% win rate but the worst total loss of any time bucket — a 0.481 SOL drain across 255 trades. The losses average 18% while the wins average only 6%. The stop loss almost never fires on these — they just slowly rot for hours before timing out.

Accepted three new ideas from the research brain: penalize the next copy-trade after a loss, blacklist the worst copy-trade wallets, and tighten exits on the 1-2 hour bleeders. The first two are parked because copy-trade has not fired in 30 days. The third (the breakeven-floor rule) is the new top priority.

Confirmed a subtle correction to the research brain's tilt analysis: when the same leader wallet fires twice in a row after a loss, the next trade is actually fairly tame (-2%). When a DIFFERENT wallet fires next, that one is the brutal one (-14%). So a per-wallet cooldown would be the wrong fix — a global half-size after any loss is the right one. Permanently filed away the per-wallet cooldown idea.

Flagged an instrumentation gap: to backtest the breakeven-floor rule properly, the bot needs to start recording the peak price reached during each trade. Right now the trade log captures only entry, exit, and final P&L. Until we have peak tracking on at least 30 trades, the breakeven-floor rule has strong logical support but no provable backtest.

novel_hypotheses.novelty: Entry-side discipline, not exit quality. Brain has only worked on exit/stop hypotheses; this is the first entry-gating proposal grounded in the trade log.
novel_hypotheses.claim: After a losing copy_trade, the very next copy_trade is dramatically worse than after a winning copy_trade.

evidence.estimated_bleed: Across the 355 next-after-loss copy trades, the gap vs the after-win baseline is on the order of 0.55 SOL of avoidable loss.

global_signal_weaker.interpretation: Tilt effect concentrates in copy_trade, not the proven strategies. Suggests copy-signal quality, not bot tilt, is the mechanism — when the leader wallets churn into a losing streak, their next signals are also bad.

novel_hypotheses.proposed_rule: After any copy_trade sell with pnl_pct < 0, apply a 30-60 min cooldown on the SAME source_wallet AND a global half-size penalty on the next copy_trade signal regardless of wallet. Re-evaluate after 50 post-rule copy_trade sells.
novel_hypotheses.estimated_value: If the rule converts the 30% WR cohort to the 42% WR baseline on half-size trades, recovers ~0.25-0.35 SOL/year at current pacing.
risks: Selection bias: copy_trade has overall 33.7% WR / no edge. A tilt rule on a no-edge strategy may just slow the bleed rather than create an edge.
The 'tilt' may actually be a clustered-bad-leader effect — same leader wallet firing twice. If so, source_wallet cooldown alone (no global penalty) is the cleaner fix.
novel_hypotheses.next_step: Owner/survival brain: split the next-after-loss cohort by same-source-wallet vs different-source-wallet. If same-wallet dominates the WR gap, the cooldown is the right fix; if different-wallet, the issue is regime-driven.

novel_hypotheses.novelty: Brain currently looks at exit reasons and emergency stops, not hold-time buckets. This is a new lens.
novel_hypotheses.claim: Trades held 0.5-1.0h have a sharp WR collapse and high SL-rate; trades held 1.0-2.0h have high WR but the WORST net SOL because winners are tiny and losers run.
key_observations: The 0.5-1h bucket WR (28.9%) is BELOW its neighbors (36.8% and 45.1%) — that's the death zone. These are trades that survived initial chop and then bled into stop.

The 1-2h bucket has the highest WR (45%) but the WORST net SOL (-0.481). SL rate is only 2.35%, meaning stops never trigger — winners are too small to cover slow bleeds. This is the 'slow loser' bucket.
proposed_rules: RULE A: Tighten time-based exit at the 50-minute mark for any open position still negative — pre-empt the 0.5-1h SL cliff.
RULE B: Add a breakeven-floor stop that ratchets up at the 60-minute mark (trailing SL at entry +0%). This forces the 1-2h slow-bleeders out at flat instead of letting them rot.
novel_hypotheses.estimated_value: If RULE B converts even 30% of the 1-2h cohort losses to breakeven, recoups ~0.10-0.14 SOL.
novel_hypotheses.next_step: Backtest RULE B on the 255-trade 1-2h bucket: simulate exit at entry+0% any time the position is open and pnl_pct >= 0 between t=60min and t=120min. Compare net pnl_sol vs actual.

novel_hypotheses.novelty: Brain's directives note 'copy_trade is on the chopping block' but no per-wallet blacklist exists. This narrows the kill rather than nuking all 537 trades worth of signal flow.
novel_hypotheses.claim: Among copy_trade source_wallets with N>=10 historical sells, 4 wallets account for disproportionate losses. A targeted blacklist is more defensible than a full kill.
caveats: Top-quartile-by-net-pnl analysis is heavily selection-biased. The proposed action is a blacklist (loss-side) not a whitelist (gain-side) for this reason.
Median 2 trades per wallet means a whitelist would be statistically empty.
novel_hypotheses.proposed_rule: Maintain a copy_trade blacklist: drop any source_wallet with N>=15 historical sells AND net_pnl_sol <= -0.020. Refresh weekly.
novel_hypotheses.next_step: Owner: pull full N>=10 wallet table from sol_trade_log.json, freeze the current bottom-4 as blacklist v1, attach to copy_trade entry gate.
